summary:
FireSight AI is an interactive Earth-observation platform that makes NASA satellite fire detections easier to understand and explore.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our project addresses the difficulty of exploring fire activity recorded by different satellite sensors, particularly MODIS and VIIRS.

Using NASA FIRMS data, FireSight AI provides interactive worldwide maps with satellite, street, and topographic backgrounds; detailed fire hotspots and activity zones; animated timelapses; and activity calendars. Users can investigate detection trends, fire radiative power, and historical observations through a dedicated research workspace.

Our persistent data library allows users to retrieve specific historical periods or import existing satellite records, making long-term exploration more accessible.

FireSight AI also highlights important scientific limitations, including differences between satellite sensors and incomplete historical coverage.

Our goal is to transform complex Earth-observation data into accessible tools that support researchers, environmental monitoring, and more informed understanding of wildfire activity worldwide.
details:
FireSight AI — Earth Fire Observatory

The Challenge

Earth-observing satellites generate valuable information about active fires, but understanding that information can be difficult.

NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments differ in their spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, observation schedules, and reporting characteristics. These differences make direct comparisons challenging, particularly when studying wildfire activity over long periods.

Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots by making satellite observations easier to explore, compare, and interpret.

Our Solution

FireSight AI is an interactive wildfire-observation and research application built around NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS).

It brings geographical visualization, satellite observations, historical exploration, and scientific analysis into one unified workspace.

Instead of navigating multiple datasets and technical interfaces, users can investigate fire activity through a single application.

Key Features

1. Interactive Global Fire Mapping

FireSight AI displays geographically referenced satellite fire detections on an interactive world map.

Users can explore hotspot locations, zoom into areas of interest, examine detection concentrations, and select activity zones for further details.

The platform offers three map backgrounds:

  • Satellite: Real-world imagery showing landscapes, forests, and urban areas.
  • Streets: Roads, cities, and infrastructure for geographical context.
  • Topography: Terrain, rivers, mountains, and landforms.

2. Fire Activity Timelapse

The interactive timelapse helps users examine changes in detected fire activity across available observation dates.

Users can play, pause, and navigate the timeline to investigate when fire detections appeared and how their geographical distribution changed.

3. MODIS and VIIRS Analysis

FireSight AI supports the exploration of observations collected by MODIS and VIIRS.

Its analytical dashboard includes sensor-specific detection counts, fire radiative power (FRP) summaries, sensor composition, and temporal activity charts.

The application distinguishes raw observation counts from scientifically calibrated comparisons, acknowledging differences in satellite detection capabilities.

4. Historical Research and Activity Calendars

Users can investigate historical wildfire observations through daily and monthly activity calendars, historical charts, and research-oriented comparisons.

Where suitable and sufficiently complete historical observations exist, the platform supports reference-period and anomaly analysis.

Missing historical data is identified rather than interpreted as zero fire activity.

5. NASA Data Library

A dedicated Data Library allows users to select geographical regions, years, months, and satellite sources for historical NASA FIRMS downloads.

Users can also import compatible CSV datasets.

Downloaded observations are stored in a persistent local SQLite database, allowing previously retrieved information to be explored again without repeating completed downloads.

6. Scientific Transparency

FireSight AI includes explanations of important scientific limitations.

Satellite hotspots represent detected thermal activity, not confirmed wildfire boundaries or burned areas. MODIS and VIIRS detection totals are not directly interchangeable without appropriate calibration and harmonization.

The platform treats irregular fire-activity zones as visualization products rather than verified fire perimeters.

Technology and Development

FireSight AI was developed using:

  • Python: Local application server, NASA data retrieval, processing, and database management.
  • JavaScript: Interactive maps, filtering, visualizations, and timelapse controls.
  • HTML and CSS: Responsive application interface and visual design.
  • SQLite: Persistent storage of imported and downloaded fire observations.
  • Leaflet: Interactive geographical mapping.
  • NASA FIRMS API: Retrieval of MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations.
  • OpenStreetMap and Esri: Street, satellite, and topographic map backgrounds.

The application runs locally through a Python server and web browser.

Innovation and Creativity

FireSight AI brings multiple aspects of satellite-fire research into one accessible interface.

Its distinguishing features include synchronized map backgrounds, geographically interactive fire-activity visualization, temporal playback, an on-demand historical data library, and explicit communication of scientific uncertainty.

Rather than hiding the limitations of satellite observations, the platform makes those limitations part of the user's research experience.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FireSight AI is intended to help students, researchers, environmental analysts, and interested communities explore satellite-detected fire activity more easily.

Potential applications include identifying seasonal observation patterns, exploring geographical concentrations, investigating historical periods, and understanding differences between satellite instruments.

By making complex Earth-observation information more accessible, FireSight AI aims to support environmental education and more informed wildfire research.

Current Status and Future Development

FireSight AI is a functional research prototype with interactive maps, timelapses, a local satellite-data library, and exploratory analysis tools.

Historical coverage depends on the NASA datasets downloaded or imported by the user. The project does not claim complete worldwide historical coverage.

Future development will focus on scientifically validated MODIS–VIIRS harmonization, more comprehensive archived observations, sensor-normalized comparisons, and improved analysis of fire trends.

Our vision is to make Earth-observation fire data easier to access, examine, and understand—while preserving the scientific context needed to interpret it responsibly.
